html:
A war between Britain and Qing China from 1839 to 1842, fought over the opium trade. China lost, and the peace forced it to open its ports to Western trade on Western terms.

Britain bought huge amounts of Chinese tea but had little that China wanted in return, so silver flowed to China. From the late 18th century British traders, many working with the East India Company, solved this by selling opium grown in India. Chinese law banned the drug, but smuggling grew fast, addiction spread and silver now flowed out of China. Under the Canton system, all Western trade had to pass through Guangzhou.

In 1839 the emperor sent the official Lin Zexu to Guangzhou to stop the trade. He seized and destroyed more than 1,000 tonnes of opium held by foreign merchants. Britain answered with a fleet. Its steam-powered warships and modern guns beat Chinese forces along the coast and up the Yangtze.

The Treaty of Nanking of 1842 made China:

  • Give Hong Kong island to Britain.
  • Open five ports, including Shanghai, to British trade and residence.
  • Pay a large indemnity and accept fixed low tariffs.

Further treaties gave Britons the right to be tried under their own law in China, and other powers soon won the same terms. The opium trade went on. Chinese historians count this war as the start of the "century of humiliation", and a Second Opium War followed from 1856 to 1860.
sum: A war between Britain and Qing China from 1839 to 1842, fought over the opium trade. China lost, and the peace forced it to open its ports to Western trade on Western terms.
